A.explanation: Gives about $9.2 \text{ N}$ if the full $F$ is used with $0.90 \text{ m}$ and signs are mishandled, ignoring that only $F\sin30^{\circ}$ is perpendicular to the bar.

B.explanation: Gives about $11 \text{ N}$ if $F\cos30^{\circ}$ is wrongly taken as the perpendicular component instead of $F\sin30^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: Balances moments about P with $F\sin30^{\circ} \times 0.90 \text{ m}$ clockwise to give a $6.0 \text{ N m}$ clockwise resultant, yielding $F = 16 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: Gives $24 \text{ N}$ if the distance $PZ$ is wrongly taken as $0.60 \text{ m}$ instead of $0.30+0.60 = 0.90 \text{ m}$.

hints: Find each perpendicular distance from pivot P: $PX = 0.30 \text{ m}$, $PY = 0.30 \text{ m}$ and $PZ = 0.30+0.60 = 0.90 \text{ m}$.
Only the component of $F$ perpendicular to bar XZ causes a moment, and $F$ is at $30^{\circ}$ to the bar axis so that component is $F\sin30^{\circ}$.
Take clockwise as positive: $16 \text{ N}$ at X and the perpendicular part of $F$ at Z act clockwise while $20 \text{ N}$ at Y acts anticlockwise, and set the sum equal to $+6.0 \text{ N m}$.
walkthrough: Distances from P are $0.30 \text{ m}$ to X, $0.30 \text{ m}$ to Y, and $0.30 \text{ m} + 0.60 \text{ m} = 0.90 \text{ m}$ to Z.

Moment is force times perpendicular distance. The $16 \text{ N}$ and $20 \text{ N}$ forces are already perpendicular, so $M_X = 16 \times 0.30 = 4.8 \text{ N m}$ and $M_Y = 20 \times 0.30 = 6.0 \text{ N m}$.
Resolve $F$: angle to bar axis is $30^{\circ}$, so perpendicular component is $F\sin30^{\circ} = 0.50F$. Its moment about P is $M_Z = 0.50F \times 0.90 = 0.45F$.
Assign signs with clockwise positive. X is left of P pushed up giving clockwise, Y is right of P pushed up giving anticlockwise, and $F$ must add clockwise to reach the stated resultant.
Write $4.8 - 6.0 + 0.45F = 6.0$. Then $0.45F = 7.2$, so $F = 7.2/0.45 = 16 \text{ N}$ with unit $\text{N}$. This is option C.
